# spa commands

Generated from `spa agent schema`. Do not edit this file; regenerate with
`spa --no-agent agent schema --markdown`. Workflows stay in the [user guide](user-guide.md).

Playbooks are not listed here. Discover them with `spa --agent run list`
and `spa run NAME --help`.

## `init`

Alias of spa environment init (spa init --example TOPOLOGY [--provider aws|virtualbox|external] NAME)

## `init list`

List topology examples. Bare spa init still scaffolds; it does not list.

Example:

```bash
spa init list
```

## `config`

Read, explain, or transactionally edit splunk_config.yml. Agents use config search QUERY, then config explain PATH. Bare spa config exits 2.

Example:

```bash
spa --agent config explain
```

## `config explain`

Describe one config path and its immediate fields. A deeper level is a longer path. The same data is the future GUI payload.

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PATH` | no | User path such as splunk_hosts or os.packages |

Example:

```bash
spa --agent config explain splunk_hosts
```

## `config search`

Find config paths. Each hit is a path and a one-line description.

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `QUERY` | yes | Search text |

Example:

```bash
spa --agent config search packages
```

## `config keys`

Catalog coverage of schema keys. Maintainer check, not the discovery walk.

Example:

```bash
spa config keys
```

## `config schema`

Human documentation generation for docs/config.md. Not an agent payload. Agents use config search QUERY, then config explain PATH.

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--markdown` | Print GitHub-flavored markdown (human stdout only; regenerate docs/config.md) |

Example:

```bash
spa --no-agent config schema --markdown
```

## `config get`

Read authored config state; pathless agent output is a compact identity outline

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--effective` | Report the schema default when the path is unset |
| `--full` | Return the full redacted authored document |

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PATH` | no | Schema path with optional identity selectors |

Example:

```bash
spa --agent config get splunk_defaults.splunk_version
```

## `config templates`

List shipped reusable config fragments and their leading summaries

Example:

```bash
spa --agent config templates
```

## `config set`

Transactionally replace one schema-backed value

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--value-file` | Read a JSON or YAML 1.2 value |
| `--from-env` | Write an environment lookup for a secret path |
| `--explicit-default` | Author a value equal to its schema default |
| `--dry-run` | Preview without writing |
| `--expect-revision` | Require the current SHA-256 revision |
| `--resolve` | Supply PATH VALUE for an unresolved dependency; repeatable |
| `--resolve-file` | Supply a sparse YAML/JSON dependency fragment |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Skip the human confirmation prompt |

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PATH` | yes | A config path. Find one: spa config search QUERY. Then read it: spa config explain PATH. Example: spa config set os.time_zone Europe/Berlin |
| `VALUE` | no | String or strict JSON value |

Example:

```bash
spa --agent config set os.time_zone Europe/Berlin
```

## `config add`

Append one new non-app identity-list entry. Fails when that identity already exists.

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--value-file` | Read a JSON or YAML 1.2 object |
| `--from-env` | FIELD NAME. Write an environment lookup for a secret field; repeatable |
| `--dry-run` | Preview without writing |
| `--expect-revision` | Require the current SHA-256 revision |
| `--resolve` | Supply PATH VALUE for an unresolved dependency; repeatable |
| `--resolve-file` | Supply a sparse YAML/JSON dependency fragment |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Skip the human confirmation prompt |

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SELECTOR` | yes | A config path for a new list entry. Find one: spa config search QUERY. Then read it: spa config explain PATH. Example: spa config add 'splunk_hosts[name=lm]' '{"roles":["license_manager"]}' |
| `JSON_OBJECT` | no | Strict JSON object for the new entry |

Example:

```bash
spa --agent config add 'splunk_hosts[name=lm]' '{"roles":["license_manager"]}'
```

## `environment init`

Scaffold or migrate an env dir; name-only uses the default parent (~/Splunk-Platform-Automator or paths.yml env_dir)

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--example` | Topology example id |
| `--provider` | Provider example: aws, virtualbox, or external (default: aws, or providers.yml) |
| `--env-dir` | One-off parent (requires --name); does not change the default parent |
| `--name` | Registry name (default: folder basename) |
| `--force` | Adopt/refresh an existing env and register it (keep splunk_config.yml unless --example) |
| `--software-dir` | Shared installers directory (saved in paths.yml) |

Example:

```bash
spa environment init --example cm_2idxc_sh my-lab
```

## `environment init list`

List topology examples (same catalog as spa init list)

Example:

```bash
spa environment init list
```

## `environment set`

User-level defaults in paths.yml (env parent, Software, baseconfig, apps) and providers.yml (only when not aws)

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--env-dir` | Default parent for name-only init |
| `--software-dir` | Shared installers directory (also sets baseconfig_dir if unset) |
| `--baseconfig-dir` | PS baseconfig apps directory |
| `--apps-dir` | Local apps directory |
| `--default` | Registered environment used when cwd does not select one |
| `--provider` | Default provider for init: aws, virtualbox, or external |

Example:

```bash
spa environment set --software-dir ~/Software --apps-dir ~/labs/apps
```


## `hosts register`

Register an existing Linux host over SSH. Does not create the machine.

Requires confirmation: yes (`--yes`).

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Confirm register |
| `--address` | IP, hostname, or FQDN. Must be reachable by SSH. |
| `--user` | SSH login user |
| `--key` | Path to the SSH private key |
| `--port` | SSH port |
| `--role` | Splunk role. Repeat to add more. |

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NAME` | yes | Inventory hostname |

Example:

```bash
spa hosts register NAME --address ADDRESS --user USER --key PATH --yes
```


## `apps content-packs list`

Inspect Content Library 5391 from --archive, apps_dir, an existing install archive, or cached pack app.conf files. An install archive is left in place. --version selects the release (default latest).

| --- | --- |

```bash

```

## `apps snippet`

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--version` | Release version (default latest) |
| `--roles` | Comma-separated target_roles (TA only) |

```bash
spa --agent apps snippet 833
```

## `apps add`

Idempotently add or update one apps[] entry; edits config and does not deploy

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--version` | Release or local archive version to author (default latest) |
| `--roles` | Comma-separated target_roles; required only for normal apps and rejected for ITSI/content packs |
| `--source` | Use Splunkbase metadata, or a folder/archive already in apps_dir (default splunkbase). Mutually exclusive with --local |
| `--local` | Shorthand for --source local. Mutually exclusive with --source |
| `--customize` | Attach an exact matching curated SPA playbook to this top-level app entry |
| `--set` | Set another schema-backed app FIELD from strict JSON; repeatable |
| `--content-pack` | 5391 only: add exact bundled folder NAME; repeatable and mutually exclusive with --install-all-content-packs |
| `--install-all-content-packs` | 5391 only: install every bundled pack; mutually exclusive with --content-pack |
| `--explicit-default` | Write omit-safe default values that SPA normally leaves absent |
| `--dry-run` | Plan dependencies and show the result without prompting or writing |
| `--expect-revision` | Write only when the config still has this SHA-256 revision |
| `--resolve` | Supply one unresolved dependency PATH VALUE; VALUE uses strict JSON; repeatable |
| `--resolve-file` | Supply unresolved dependencies from sparse YAML/JSON; use - for stdin |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Skip the human config-edit confirmation; agent mode never prompts |

Example:

```bash
spa --agent apps add 833 --roles search_head,indexer
```

| `--resolve` | Supply PATH VALUE for an unresolved dependency; repeatable |
| `--resolve-file` | Supply a sparse YAML/JSON dependency fragment |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Skip the human confirmation prompt |

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `APP_ID_OR_NAME` | yes | A Splunkbase id or an app name in this config. Find one: spa apps search QUERY. Example: spa apps remove 833 |

Example:

```bash
spa --agent apps remove 833
```

## `apps download`

Download a Splunkbase archive into apps_dir (does not edit config or print a snippet)

Requires confirmation: yes (`--yes`).

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Confirm download (required in agent mode) |
| `--version` | Release version (default latest) |
| `--extract` | Safely extract a folder-backed app into apps_dir and delete the archive (TA/ES only) |
| `--overwrite` | With --extract, replace an existing app folder in apps_dir |

Example:

```bash
spa apps download 833 --yes
```

## `agent schema`

This schema (JSON envelope; --markdown prints a human catalog)

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--markdown` | Print GitHub-flavored markdown instead of JSON (human stdout; regenerate docs/commands.md) |

Example:

```bash
spa --no-agent agent schema --markdown
```

## `completion`

Print a bash or zsh completion function. Human shell setup. Bare spa completion exits 2. Agents use spa agent schema.

Example:

```bash
spa completion zsh
```

## `completion bash`

Print a bash function for eval. Does not edit the shell startup file. Agents use spa agent schema.

Example:

```bash
spa completion bash
```

## `completion zsh`

Print a zsh function for eval. Does not edit the shell startup file. Agents use spa agent schema.

Example:

```bash
spa completion zsh
```
